articles.title: One Of America’s Greatest Judges Ditched An Even More Unique First Name
articles.content:
Ed. Note: Welcome to our daily feature Trivia Question of the Day!

“Learned Hand” is one of the most memorable names in American law — a brilliant federal appeals judge, the most-quoted jurist never to sit on the Supreme Court, owner of a moniker that sounds almost too good to be real. But “Learned” wasn’t his first name at all; it was his middle name, taken from his mother’s side of the family. What was the given first name he was born with — and later dropped?

Hint: As Professor Orin Kerr is fond of noting, Hand’s given first name is exceedingly appropriate for a lawyer.

See the answer on the next page.

The post One Of America’s Greatest Judges Ditched An Even More Unique First Name appeared first on Above the Law.

articles.title: Harvey Now Connects To Legal Research Platform Midpage Through An MCP Connector
articles.content:
The connector makes Midpage’s research library of U.S. case law, statutes, regulations, and agency materials accessible from directly within Harvey, so lawyers can find and cite authority on the same platform they use for drafting and analysis.
Harvey customers can run Midpage searches from Harvey Assistant threads, with cited sources delivered in the final output, the companies said.
They offered these examples of how you can use this:
- Research memos: Ask a legal question in Harvey, search Midpage, and pull the relevant opinions and key passages into the memo.
- Briefs and motions: Find supporting authority while drafting, with quoted passages drawn from the source opinion.
- Citation review: Check that the authorities cited in a draft exist and support the point they are cited for.
- Statutory and regulatory questions: Search statutes, regulations, and agency materials alongside case law when advising clients.
To take advantage of the connector, users must be customers of both Harvey and Midpage.
“Our customers keep asking for Midpage wherever they work, and many of them draft and analyze in Harvey,” said Otto Zastrow, founder and CEO of Midpage. “Now the research and the drafting happen on one platform, and every proposition can be traced to the authority behind it.”
The Midpage connector is now available in Harvey’s Connector Library.

articles.title: Arizona Supreme Court Says Yes To A Law School Outside The ABA’s Accreditation System
articles.content:
Ed. note: Welcome to our daily feature, Quote of the Day.
We are grateful for the Arizona Supreme Court’s willingness to consider an innovative approach to legal education and for the opportunity to demonstrate that a new pathway to licensure can maintain the highest standards of academic excellence, professional preparation and ethical responsibility. We recognize the significance of being the first institution to operate under these standards and the responsibility that comes with it.
— James L. Williams, dean of Grand Canyon University’s College of Law, in comments given after the Arizona Supreme Court unanimously approved the school as the state’s first non-ABA-accredited law school. The approval gives graduates a path to seek admission to the Arizona bar, provided they meet the state’s other licensing requirements. Chief Justice Ann A. Scott Timmer said Arizona faces “a significant shortage of attorneys” and expressed optimism that GCU could help meet the need. GCU President Brian Mueller said the university welcomes the court’s oversight and the chance to show that “innovation in higher education and rigorous professional standards can go hand in hand.” GCU plans to pursue ABA accreditation once eligible; under current rules, its graduates may have limited options to practice outside Arizona.
